tasks.task: Establish site, confirm services isolation plan
tasks.scope: Set up site boundaries, confirm electrical and HVAC isolation strategy with services coordinator, establish exclusion zones for demolition face and occupied floors below, erect hoarding and barricades to separate work area from adjacent operational tenancies.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Uncontrolled electrical supply to HVAC or other building services — risk of electrocution during isolation work or accidental re-energisation
Unconfirmed service isolation strategy — risk of inadvertent disruption to occupied floors or building utilities
tasks.dominant_hazard: Uncontrolled electrical supply — risk of electrocution
controls: Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any hoardings or permit unauthorised access until: exclusion zone boundaries are confirmed in writing by PM and all personnel briefed on access restrictions
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: electrical mains disconnection certificate cannot be obtained before site setup, or if building services cannot be isolated as per written strategy

🛑 STOP WORK if: building management advises that HVAC or other services serving occupied floors cannot be isolated without disruption — refer to structural engineer and project manager for revised isolation sequence
admin: Verify all site personnel hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) — maintain register on site.
tell building management and adjacent tenants 48 hours before site setup — confirm occupation schedule and emergency contact details.
Establish daily communication protocol with building management about isolation status and access restrictions.
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: Before site setup commences, daily check of isolation tags and hoarding integrity
monitoring.evidence: Disconnection certificate retained on file; isolation tag register updated daily; photographic record of hoarding installation and exclusion zone signage

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Demolish existing partition walls and ceiling grid
tasks.scope: Remove gyprock partitions, timber/metal frames, suspended ceiling grid, and panels. Confirm absence of asbestos via provided clearance certificate. Manage dust and debris within hoarding. Load and remove debris to skip bin. Establish falling-object exclusion zone for full height of demolition face plus 5m below.
hazards: Collapse or uncontrolled fall of partition wall or ceiling grid section — risk of crush injury to personnel
Asbestos fibre release if clearance certificate is not valid or if disturbed material is not confirmed asbestos-free — risk of mesothelioma or lung disease
Struck-by injury from power tools or hand tools during wall and grid dismantling — risk of laceration or fracture
tasks.dominant_hazard: Falling debris — risk of serious head injury or death
controls: Wet-suppress gyprock and ceiling panels during removal to suppress dust — do not allow dry breakout or dust generation above containment.
Install temporary propping or bracing on load-bearing partition frames before removal commences — no unauthorised cutting or sudden load release.
Use dust extraction or on-tool dust capture during any grinding, cutting, or power-tool use — maintain RPE if dust cannot be suppressed.
Load debris directly into skip bin from containment hoarding — do not throw or drop debris from height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove load-bearing partition frame until: engineer-approved temporary propping is installed, inspected, and signed off.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: debris escapes containment hoarding or personnel breach falling-object exclusion zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unplanned structural movement, cracking, or load instability is observed in remaining building elements or temporary props.
admin: Provide engineer-approved temporary propping or bracing plan before load-bearing partition removal.
Brief workers on exclusion zone, falling-object risk, asbestos trigger, and stop-work conditions.
ppe: Hard hat (mandatory — full shift in demolition zone and exclusion zone below).
Organic vapour + particulate respirator (P2 equivalent or higher) — mandatory if dust suppression fails or dry breakout occurs.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone maintained — no unauthorised personnel entry; debris contained within hoarding.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during demolition; pre-shift check of hoarding and signage.
monitoring.evidence: Zone barricades intact and visible; no debris outside containment; exclusion zone log maintained; asbestos certificate sighted and dated.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Demolish existing partition walls and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Demolish existing partition walls and per SWMS

tasks.task: Expose and prepare structural ceiling substrate
tasks.scope: Remove loose material, dust, and debris from exposed slab soffit. Check for cracks, spalling, or surface damage. Report any structural concerns to project manager before proceeding. Brush clean and allow substrate to settle before installing new ceiling system.
hazards: Dust and debris exposure during cleaning and loose-material removal — risk of respiratory irritation or inhalation of fine particles
Falling debris or loose material from slab soffit during cleaning — risk of head or eye injury
Structural damage not identified — risk of collapse or sudden failure during subsequent ceiling installation if cracks or spalling are not correctly reported
tasks.dominant_hazard: Unidentified structural damage leading to collapse during installation
controls: Obtain structural engineer's written approval before starting work — confirm slab soffit can safely support temporary ceiling load and inspection activity.
Wet all loose material and dust on slab soffit using spray bottle or damp cloth — do not dry sweep or brush.
Remove loose debris by hand into labelled waste bag — do not force material; stop if material will not separate cleanly.
Check entire slab soffit surface for cracks wider than 2 mm, spalling deeper than 10 mm, rust staining, or water damage — mark each defect with tape and photograph.
Brief all workers on hazard: structural defects must be reported before ceiling work proceeds — do not assume defects are minor.
Do not cover or hide any structural defect with new material — all defects must be visible to project manager and engineer.
Allow substrate to air dry for minimum 24 hours after cleaning — verify no active moisture or seepage before signing off.
Provide report to project manager listing all defects found, location, size, and photographs — obtain PM sign-off before proceeding to ceiling installation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install ceiling system until: structural engineer has inspected and approved all identified defects in writing and PM has authorized method to proceed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: slab soffit shows signs of active structural movement, settlement, or failure during cleaning.
🛑 STOP WORK if: cracks wider than 5 mm or spalling deeper than 25 mm are found — engineer re-assessment required.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water seepage, active moisture, or structural decay is present — substrate cannot be certified as safe for load.
admin: Complete structural defect register with photographs and measurements before submission to PM.
Brief all site personnel that this is a structural-critical task — defect reporting is a no-fault safety hold.
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (organic vapour if mould present — confirm with SDS before use)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before task start; before ceiling installation
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer approval letter or inspection certificate; defect register with photographs and PM sign-off

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Expose and prepare structural ceiling
responsibility.WKR: Perform Expose and prepare structural ceiling per SWMS

tasks.task: Install new suspended ceiling grid and hangers
tasks.scope: Locate and confirm ceiling anchor points in structural slab. Install hanger wires or spring anchors at spacing per design drawings. Erect perimeter and main runners at correct height and alignment. Confirm grid is level and stable before panel installation.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance or slips while working at ceiling height on ladders or scaffolding — risk of serious injury or death
Hanger wire failure or incorrect installation — risk of ceiling grid collapse during or after installation
Struck-by injury from ceiling components, tools, or equipment during installation — risk of laceration or fracture
Entanglement hazard from hanger wire or spring anchor components — risk of trapped hand or arm during handling
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during ceiling installation
controls: Install and secure ladder or mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) on level ground before ascending to ceiling height.
Confirm all anchor points in structural slab are sound and rated for design load before installing first hanger wire.
Install hanger wires or spring anchors at spacing and load rating per design drawings; do not deviate from spacing or anchor type.
Wear safety harness with lanyard anchored to independent fixed point if working above 2 m and fall protection cannot be guaranteed by platform edge.
Install edge protection or guardrail around elevated work platform; maintain clear 1.2 m exclusion zone below ceiling work.
Check hanger wire and spring anchor components for damage, corrosion, or defect before installation; do not use damaged items.
Level and align perimeter and main runners using spirit level and laser alignment tool before fixing secondary hangers.
Barricade floor area below work; post warning sign 'Ceiling Installation in Progress — Do Not Enter'.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install hanger wires until: structural engineer or supervisor confirms all anchor points are located, exposed, and rated for design load on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install ceiling panels until: grid alignment and levelling is confirmed by supervisor and documented (written sign-off or photo record).
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: hanger wire is cracked, corroded, kinked, or shows visible defect before or during installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any anchor point is crumbling, loose, or does not support test load without movement.
🛑 STOP WORK if: grid is not level (tolerance >10 mm over 3 m) or shows visible sag or misalignment after installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain site induction (White Card CPCCWHS1001) and confirm understanding of fall prevention and suspended load hazards.
Confirm occupied building protocols: liaison with building manager, restriction of work hours, and exclusion of building occupants from work area.
Keep design drawings and hanger spacing schedule on site and visible during installation.
Record hanger installation locations and load test results in site log or photo record for final inspection.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Safety harness and shock-absorber lanyard (if working above 2 m without edge protection guardrail)

monitoring.critical_control: Check all hanger wires and anchor points for damage or loose components before and during installation.
monitoring.frequency: Before each work shift; continuous during installation; before moving to next grid section
monitoring.evidence: Visual check recorded in site diary or photo log; hanger installation schedule ticked off per location; final grid level sign-off by supervisor

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install new suspended ceiling grid
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install new suspended ceiling grid per SWMS

tasks.task: Install ceiling panels, gyprock facing, and seals
tasks.scope: Install suspended ceiling tiles or panels into grid framework. Install gyprock sheets to partition frames. Seal all partition-to-soffit gaps and service penetrations with fire-rated sealant. Joint tape and finish gyprock seams per specification. Allow compound to cure
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance on ladder or platform while lifting ceiling panels or gyprock sheets — risk of serious injury or death
Gyprock sheet or panel falls from height or during handling — risk of crush injury or head injury to personnel below
Chemical burn from fire-rated sealant contact with skin — risk of dermatitis or respiratory irritation if fumes are inhaled
Muscle strain or back injury during manual handling and installation of heavy gyprock panels — risk of soft-tissue injury or acute strain
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during panel or gyprock installation
controls: Install and secure work platform or scaffolding to grid height before starting. Platform must be stable, level, and rated for full crew weight plus material loads.
Erect exclusion zone below work area. Barricade 2 m radius around all panel and gyprock handling. Post spotter to control access and watch for dropped objects.
check ladder or step stool for damage or defects before use. Secure ladder base with feet on level ground. Only single-person access allowed on ladders.
Wear harness and lanyard clipped to overhead anchor point rated for work load during elevated work above 2 m height.
Check fire-rated sealant SDS on point of use before opening. Confirm ventilation in area is adequate — open windows or activate local exhaust fan.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and hi-viz shirt or vest
Use two-person team for gyprock sheet handling. Use lifting frame or mechanical hoist to raise sheets to height. Never manually lift gyprock above shoulder height.
Secure ceiling panels and gyprock sheets to grid or frame immediately after installation. Do not leave unsupported material at height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install panels or gyprock until: work platform is installed, level, secured, and tagged as safe by supervisor
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply fire-rated sealant until: substrate is clean and dry, SDS Section 8 ventilation requirements are confirmed on site, and chemical PPE is available and worn
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses footing on platform or ladder, or harness anchor point fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: gyprock sheet or panel becomes unstable, drops, or shows signs of falling
🛑 STOP WORK if: sealant fumes cannot be controlled by ventilation or worker reports respiratory irritation or skin contact occurs
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all crew on hazards, control method, and exclusion zone boundaries before work starts.
Confirm building occupants are notified of ceiling work, exclusion zone, and sealant cure time before starting.
Record work completion, cure time start, and re-entry approval date on site log.
White Card (CPCCWHS1001) verification — general construction induction completed by all workers on site.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Hard hat — mandatory for all personnel on site during elevated work
Safety harness and lanyard — mandatory for workers above 2 m height
hi-viz shirt or vest— mandatory when handling gyprock or applying sealant
Organic vapour respirator (cartridge-type, per SDS Section 8) — mandatory if sealant ventilation is inadequate or fumes are detected
steel-capped footwear— steel-capped boots with slip-resistant sole

monitoring.critical_control: SDS reviewed for product hazards, RPE matched to SDS requirements (organic vapour cartridge for solvents, not P2 dust mask), ventilation confirmed operational
monitoring.frequency: Before each work shift starts, continuous visual monitoring during work
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor sign-off on platform inspection checklist; harness and lanyard visual check; exclusion zone maintained and clear of unauthorised entry

responsibility.SUP: Verify SDS on site, check ventilation, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Apply sealant per specification, wear PPE, report chemical exposure

tasks.task: Remove fixtures, fittings, and mechanical plant from Level 3
tasks.scope: Disconnect and remove light fittings, outlet boxes, grilles, HVAC diffusers, and terminal units before partition and ceiling demolition. Coordinate with services trades. Cap or plug all service openings. Tag and store reusable components.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Exposure to remaining electrical supply in outlet boxes or light fittings — risk of shock or electrocution if not isolated before disconnect
Uncontrolled release of HVAC refrigerant or compressed gas during disconnection — risk of chemical burn or inhalation injury
Falling light fittings or terminal units from height — risk of head injury to personnel below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Electrical shock during disconnection of energised fittings
controls: Isolate HVAC terminal units and diffusers from supply air and return air ducts; cap or plug all openings immediately after disconnection to prevent dust and debris entry.
Obtain HVAC disconnection certificate from services trade confirming refrigerant and compressed gas systems are depressurised and safely vented before terminal unit removal.
Secure light fittings with rope or strap before loosening final fixings; lower fittings hand-over-hand to ground level — do not drop or swing fittings over occupied areas.
Barricade and delineate the removal zone below all elevated work on Level 3 to prevent unauthorised entry; post 'Removal in Progress' signs at all access points.
Brief all site personnel on Level 3 that fixture and plant removal is in progress; confirm no unauthorised entry to the removal zone and coordinate with concurrent occupied-building activities.
Tag all reusable components with project ID and storage location before removal; store safely in designated area away from pedestrian and vehicle traffic.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: voltage is detected on any outlet box or fitting during verification testing — do not proceed until electrical coordinator re-isolates and re-certifies.
🛑 STOP WORK if: HVAC refrigerant or gas disconnection certificate cannot be obtained before terminal unit removal — contact services coordinator immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: barricade or exclusion zone is breached or removal zone is entered by unauthorised personnel during active removal work.
admin: Obtain HVAC disconnection certificate from services trade confirming safe venting and depressurisation.
Coordinate removal schedule with building services and facilities teams; confirm no concurrent electrical or mechanical work is in progress on Level 3.
ppe: Safety helmet (hard hat) — mandatory when working below or adjacent to elevated removals.
eye protection— mandatory when disconnecting electrical outlets or HVAC ducts.
High-visibility vest — mandatory in the removal zone.
steel-capped footwear— mandatory on Level 3 during removal operations.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each fixture/fitting disconnection
monitoring.evidence: Electrical isolation certificate on-site; multi-meter test log; photograph of de-energised outlet and fitting tags

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove fixtures, fittings, and mechanical
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove fixtures, fittings, and mechanical per SWMS

tasks.task: Install new partition walls and timber frames
tasks.scope: Erect floor-to-ceiling gyprock partitions along marked lines. Install top and bottom plates, studs, and noggins per design drawings. Confirm vertical and horizontal alignment. Install service access holes as marked. Do not install gyprock facing until frames are inspected and approved.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance on ladder or scaffold while installing top plates or upper studs — risk of serious injury or death
Partition frame collapse during installation if not adequately braced — risk of crush injury to personnel
Struck-by injury from falling timber or studs during frame erection — risk of head or upper-body injury
Muscle strain or back injury during manual handling of heavy timber frames or stud lengths — risk of soft-tissue injury
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during partition frame installation
controls: Erect mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) or secure ladder to stable base before installing top plates above 2m height.
Install temporary horizontal bracing between studs at mid-height and top during frame erection to prevent collapse or sideways movement.
Wear safety harness with lanyard attached to fixed anchor point when working above 2m on scaffold or MEWP.
Brief all workers on partition layout and marked service access holes before timber delivery and frame start.
Confirm vertical and horizontal alignment with laser level or spirit level after every second stud is secured.
Use mechanical handling aid (trolley, dolly) to move stud lengths and frame assemblies; carry only short timber lengths by hand.
Barricade and delineate partition work area to exclude site personnel not involved in frame erection.
Position timber stacks flat and stable, no higher than 1.5m, away from edge of work platform or scaffold.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install top plates above 2m height until: ladder or MEWP is installed, secured, and tagged.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install gyprock facing until: project supervisor or structural engineer confirms vertical and horizontal alignment, bracing is complete, and service holes are cut and clear.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: frame shows visible lateral movement, temporary bracing loosens or shifts, or unauthorised removal of bracing occurs.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses footing or stability on ladder or MEWP, or harness becomes detached or slack.
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupants or site personnel enter barricaded work area or partition layout differs materially from marked design.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain design drawings and confirm marked partition lines and service hole locations on site before frame material delivery.
Confirm manual handling loads; if any single stud or frame section exceeds 20 kg, assign two workers or use mechanical aid.
Record frame installation progress and alignment confirmation (date, worker name, level) in site diary before moving to next partition.
Coordinate with building occupants; advise of work area boundaries and restrict access during frame erection.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (when working above 2m)
Dust mask (P2) when drilling service access holes

monitoring.critical_control: SDS reviewed for product hazards, RPE matched to SDS requirements (organic vapour cartridge for solvents, not P2 dust mask), ventilation confirmed operational
monitoring.who: Site supervisor or nominated worker induction authority
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift and each time worker enters MEWP or climbs ladder above 2m
monitoring.evidence: Harness tag and lanyard visual check; worker acknowledgment in toolbox talk record

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install new partition walls and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install new partition walls and per SWMS

tasks.task: Coordinate and install services routes and terminations
tasks.scope: Work with electrical, data, and HVAC trades to route cables, conduits, and ductwork through partition cavities and above ceiling grid. Install outlet boxes, data points, and grille supports as per services design. Complete all service rough-ins before gyprock facing commences.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Electrocution — contact with energised electrical cable or conduit during routing or termination — risk of shock or death if cable is not isolated or identified
Struck-by injury from suspended cable or ductwork during installation — risk of head or facial injury
Pinch-point or crush injury to fingers and hands during ductwork or cable-tray assembly — risk of fracture or crush injury
Coordination failure between trades — risk of rework, delay, and repeat exposure to hazards if electrical, data, and HVAC routes conflict
controls: Verify all electrical, data, and HVAC trade routes on marked-up floor plan and 3D model before any installation starts. Resolve conflicts on site with all trades present and document agreement in writing.
Use cable identification tape (colour-coded per AS/NZS 3000) at all cable entry and exit points. Do not route unmarked cable.
Install electrical conduit or cable tray before pulling cable. Do not lay exposed cable in partition cavities or ceiling voids.
Secure all suspended ductwork and cable trays with approved hangers every 1.2 m. Check that hangers are anchored to structural members, not partition frames or services.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (Level 5) and eye protection, conduit, and ductwork edges. Change gloves if cut or torn.
Establish exclusion zone (2 m radius) below all overhead service installation work. Restrict access to authorised workers and alert occupants before work starts.
Brief all trades on pinch-point and crush hazards during ductwork assembly. Demonstrate safe hand position and clearance zone around bending and joining operations.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not route any electrical cable until: licensed electrician has issued isolation certificate confirming cable de-energised and locked-off at source, and plan conflicts have been resolved and documented
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start gyprock facing until: all service rough-ins complete, tested, and signed off in writing by electrical, data, and HVAC trade leads
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unmarked, unidentified, or suspected energised cable is encountered during routing or termination
🛑 STOP WORK if: trade routes conflict on site and cannot be resolved immediately with all trades present
🛑 STOP WORK if: any suspended ductwork or cable tray anchor point shifts, loosens, or shows visible damage during or after installation
admin: Obtain marked-up floor plans and 3D services model from design engineer before work starts.
Schedule pre-installation coordination meeting with electrical, data, and HVAC trade leads. Document agreed routes and sequence.
Maintain cable identification record (location, colour, route, de-energised date, electrician sign-off) on site.
Record all trade sign-offs on service rough-in completion checklist before gyprock commences.
Brief all occupants in building areas where overhead service work is occurring. Display exclusion zone signage.
Report any hazmat discovery (asbestos-containing insulation, lead paint on cable conduit) to project manager immediately.
ppe: High-visibility vest (occupied building, near occupant movement)
Hard hat (ceiling cavity work, suspended load risk)

monitoring.critical_control: Scaffold or EWP daily pre-use check completed, documented, no visible defects
monitoring.who: Site supervisor and electrical trade lead
monitoring.frequency: Before each service routing task and each cable termination
monitoring.evidence: Signed isolation certificate on site, visual inspection of cable de-energisation tester reading, trade sign-off log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Coordinate and install services routes
responsibility.WKR: Perform Coordinate and install services routes per SWMS

tasks.task: Install carpet tiles and floor finishes
tasks.scope: Prepare floor substrate — vacuum, remove all dust and debris. Install underlay if required. Lay carpet tiles in specified pattern from centre point outward. Trim edge tiles to suit perimeter and service penetrations. Secure tiles as per manufacturer specification.
hazards: Trip hazard from debris, underlay folds, or uneven floor substrate — risk of slip and fall causing minor injury or fracture
Muscle strain or back injury during kneeling, bending, and manual laying of carpet tiles — risk of soft-tissue injury or acute strain
Exposure to adhesive or bonding-agent fumes during tile installation — risk of respiratory irritation or chemical sensitivity
tasks.dominant_hazard: Muscle strain or back injury during repetitive installation work
controls: Clear and vacuum floor substrate thoroughly before underlay or tile placement — remove all dust, debris, and loose material.
check floor surface for levelness, cracks, or damage — tell supervisor if substrate varies >3 mm over 3 m or is unsuitable for tile installation.
Lay underlay smoothly without folds or wrinkles — secure edges and seams to prevent trip hazards during tile installation.
Start tile layout from marked centre point — establish grid pattern and confirm alignment before securing any tiles.
Kneel on tile-laying board or kneeling pad — do not work on bare concrete or hard surfaces for extended periods.
Limit repetitive bending and kneeling — rotate task every 30 minutes with posture-neutral task (e.g., measuring, trimming, material staging).
Use handheld tile cutter for edge trims — cut tiles over debris tray to contain dust and fragments; never bend or force tiles by hand.
Apply adhesive or bonding agent per manufacturer SDS — make sure room is ventilated, SDS on point of use, and application limits adhered to.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install underlay or start tiling until: floor substrate is clean, dry, inspected, and levelness confirmed as suitable for installation.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: floor substrate is uneven (>3 mm variation over 3 m), cracked, contaminated, or wet — do not proceed until rectified and approved.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails during adhesive application or room becomes unoccupiable due to fume buildup — resume only when air quality is restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports back pain, muscle strain, or repetitive-strain symptoms — assign alternative task and review work pace and posture.
admin: Confirm building occupancy and public access — brief occupants on restricted floor areas and cure time before re-entry.
Obtain SDS for tile adhesive or bonding agent — review Section 8 (exposure control) and Section 16 (health hazard) before tile installation starts.
Document tile layout pattern and centre-point mark — photograph and brief all workers before installation commences.
Record cure times and re-entry restrictions on site signage — post 'Do Not Walk — Curing Tiles' notices until manufacturer cure period is met.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) — if adhesive vapour levels exceed manufacturer threshold or room ventilation is limited.
Safety shoes with good grip — for wet or adhesive-contaminated floor areas.
Knee pads — for kneeling work on hard floors and underlay.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each use
monitoring.evidence: Worker confirmation and visual check of extraction hose and respirator seal
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Worker confirmation and visual check of extraction hose and respirator seal

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install carpet tiles and floor
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install carpet tiles and floor per SWMS

tasks.task: Reinstall light fittings, grilles, and access panels
tasks.scope: Install and connect light fittings and outlets to completed electrical rough-in. Fit HVAC diffusers and grilles to completed ductwork. Install access panels to ceiling grid. Test all fittings for secure mounting and functionality.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Electrocution — contact with energised electrical connections or incorrectly isolated supply during light fitting installation — risk of shock or death
Fall from height — worker loses balance on ladder while installing ceiling fittings — risk of serious injury or death
Falling light fitting or grille during installation — risk of head or upper-body injury to personnel below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Electrocution during connection of light fittings to energised supply
controls: Verify electrical supply to light circuit is isolated at switchboard and padlocked before opening any fitting or connection point.
Confirm isolation using a two-point voltage tester on the circuit before touching any conductor or terminal.
Install light fittings and connect to isolated rough-in only. Do not work on energised circuits.
Check each light fitting for secure mounting to ceiling structure before energising circuit.
Test fitting functionality after energisation only when all personnel have vacated the area directly below.
Install HVAC grilles and diffusers to completed ductwork using specified fixing method — verify no loose components before leaving work area.
Position ladder on stable, level ground. Keep ladder at 75° angle. Do not overreach — move ladder instead.
Barricade area directly below ceiling work to prevent unauthorised entry during fitting installation and testing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not energise any light circuit until: electrical rough-in has been checked for continuity and earth integrity by the electrician, and isolation and two-point test have been verified and recorded by supervisor on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: voltage tester shows supply is not fully isolated before any connection work begins.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ladder becomes unstable, unsecured, or personnel attempt to work from ladder at angle less than 70° or greater than 80°.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupied building personnel enter the barricaded area below ceiling work.
admin: Obtain site isolation permit confirming electrical supply isolation and padlock placement before work starts.
Brief all personnel on barricade location and entry prohibition during fitting installation and testing phase.
Record circuit isolation, two-point test result, and fitting functionality test in site logbook with date, time, and tester name.
tell building manager and occupants of temporary supply isolation and expected duration.

monitoring.critical_control: Two-point voltage test on isolated circuit — negative result on both test points before any conductor contact.
monitoring.frequency: Before opening any fitting connection point; before energising each circuit after installation
monitoring.evidence: Site logbook entry: date, time, circuit identification, tester name, test result (pass/fail), supervisor sign-off

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points

tasks.task: Conduct final inspection and defect rectification

task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove loose material, dust, and debris from exposed slab soffit. Check for cracks, spalling, or surface damage. Report any structural concerns to project manager before proceeding. Brush clean and allow substrate to settle before installing new ceiling system.
hazards: Dust and debris exposure during cleaning and loose-material removal — risk of respiratory irritation or inhalation of fine particles
Falling debris or loose material from slab soffit during cleaning — risk of head or eye injury
Structural damage not identified — risk of collapse or sudden failure during subsequent ceiling installation if cracks or spalling are not correctly reported
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Unidentified structural damage leading to collapse during installation
controls: Obtain structural engineer's written approval before starting work — confirm slab soffit can safely support temporary ceiling load and inspection activity.
Wet all loose material and dust on slab soffit using spray bottle or damp cloth — do not dry sweep or brush.
Remove loose debris by hand into labelled waste bag — do not force material; stop if material will not separate cleanly.
Check entire slab soffit surface for cracks wider than 2 mm, spalling deeper than 10 mm, rust staining, or water damage — mark each defect with tape and photograph.
Brief all workers on hazard: structural defects must be reported before ceiling work proceeds — do not assume defects are minor.
Do not cover or hide any structural defect with new material — all defects must be visible to project manager and engineer.
Allow substrate to air dry for minimum 24 hours after cleaning — verify no active moisture or seepage before signing off.
Provide report to project manager listing all defects found, location, size, and photographs — obtain PM sign-off before proceeding to ceiling installation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install ceiling system until: structural engineer has inspected and approved all identified defects in writing and PM has authorized method to proceed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: slab soffit shows signs of active structural movement, settlement, or failure during cleaning.
🛑 STOP WORK if: cracks wider than 5 mm or spalling deeper than 25 mm are found — engineer re-assessment required.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water seepage, active moisture, or structural decay is present — substrate cannot be certified as safe for load.
admin: Complete structural defect register with photographs and measurements before submission to PM.
Brief all site personnel that this is a structural-critical task — defect reporting is a no-fault safety hold.
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (organic vapour if mould present — confirm with SDS before use)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before task start; before ceiling installation
monitoring.evidence: Signed engineer approval letter or inspection certificate; defect register with photographs and PM sign-off

task_blocks_raw.task: Install new suspended ceiling grid and hangers
task_blocks_raw.scope: Locate and confirm ceiling anchor points in structural slab. Install hanger wires or spring anchors at spacing per design drawings. Erect perimeter and main runners at correct height and alignment. Confirm grid is level and stable before panel installation.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance or slips while working at ceiling height on ladders or scaffolding — risk of serious injury or death
Hanger wire failure or incorrect installation — risk of ceiling grid collapse during or after installation
Struck-by injury from ceiling components, tools, or equipment during installation — risk of laceration or fracture
Entanglement hazard from hanger wire or spring anchor components — risk of trapped hand or arm during handling
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during ceiling installation
controls: Install and secure ladder or mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) on level ground before ascending to ceiling height.
Confirm all anchor points in structural slab are sound and rated for design load before installing first hanger wire.
Install hanger wires or spring anchors at spacing and load rating per design drawings; do not deviate from spacing or anchor type.
Wear safety harness with lanyard anchored to independent fixed point if working above 2 m and fall protection cannot be guaranteed by platform edge.
Install edge protection or guardrail around elevated work platform; maintain clear 1.2 m exclusion zone below ceiling work.
Check hanger wire and spring anchor components for damage, corrosion, or defect before installation; do not use damaged items.
Level and align perimeter and main runners using spirit level and laser alignment tool before fixing secondary hangers.
Barricade floor area below work; post warning sign 'Ceiling Installation in Progress — Do Not Enter'.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install hanger wires until: structural engineer or supervisor confirms all anchor points are located, exposed, and rated for design load on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install ceiling panels until: grid alignment and levelling is confirmed by supervisor and documented (written sign-off or photo record).
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: hanger wire is cracked, corroded, kinked, or shows visible defect before or during installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any anchor point is crumbling, loose, or does not support test load without movement.
🛑 STOP WORK if: grid is not level (tolerance >10 mm over 3 m) or shows visible sag or misalignment after installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Confirm occupied building protocols: liaison with building manager, restriction of work hours, and exclusion of building occupants from work area.
Keep design drawings and hanger spacing schedule on site and visible during installation.
Record hanger installation locations and load test results in site log or photo record for final inspection.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.frequency: Before each work shift; continuous during installation; before moving to next grid section
monitoring.evidence: Visual check recorded in site diary or photo log; hanger installation schedule ticked off per location; final grid level sign-off by supervisor

task_blocks_raw.task: Install new partition walls and timber frames
task_blocks_raw.scope: Erect floor-to-ceiling gyprock partitions along marked lines. Install top and bottom plates, studs, and noggins per design drawings. Confirm vertical and horizontal alignment. Install service access holes as marked. Do not install gyprock facing until frames are inspected and approved.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance on ladder or scaffold while installing top plates or upper studs — risk of serious injury or death
Partition frame collapse during installation if not adequately braced — risk of crush injury to personnel
Struck-by injury from falling timber or studs during frame erection — risk of head or upper-body injury
Muscle strain or back injury during manual handling of heavy timber frames or stud lengths — risk of soft-tissue injury
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during partition frame installation
controls: Erect mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) or secure ladder to stable base before installing top plates above 2m height.
Install temporary horizontal bracing between studs at mid-height and top during frame erection to prevent collapse or sideways movement.
Wear safety harness with lanyard attached to fixed anchor point when working above 2m on scaffold or MEWP.
Brief all workers on partition layout and marked service access holes before timber delivery and frame start.
Confirm vertical and horizontal alignment with laser level or spirit level after every second stud is secured.
Use mechanical handling aid (trolley, dolly) to move stud lengths and frame assemblies; carry only short timber lengths by hand.
Barricade and delineate partition work area to exclude site personnel not involved in frame erection.
Position timber stacks flat and stable, no higher than 1.5m, away from edge of work platform or scaffold.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install top plates above 2m height until: ladder or MEWP is installed, secured, and tagged.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install gyprock facing until: project supervisor or structural engineer confirms vertical and horizontal alignment, bracing is complete, and service holes are cut and clear.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: frame shows visible lateral movement, temporary bracing loosens or shifts, or unauthorised removal of bracing occurs.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses footing or stability on ladder or MEWP, or harness becomes detached or slack.
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupants or site personnel enter barricaded work area or partition layout differs materially from marked design.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain design drawings and confirm marked partition lines and service hole locations on site before frame material delivery.
Confirm manual handling loads; if any single stud or frame section exceeds 20 kg, assign two workers or use mechanical aid.
Record frame installation progress and alignment confirmation (date, worker name, level) in site diary before moving to next partition.
Coordinate with building occupants; advise of work area boundaries and restrict access during frame erection.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (when working above 2m)
Dust mask (P2) when drilling service access holes

task_blocks_raw.task: Coordinate and install services routes and terminations
task_blocks_raw.scope: Work with electrical, data, and HVAC trades to route cables, conduits, and ductwork through partition cavities and above ceiling grid. Install outlet boxes, data points, and grille supports as per services design. Complete all service rough-ins before gyprock facing commences.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Electrocution — contact with energised electrical cable or conduit during routing or termination — risk of shock or death if cable is not isolated or identified
Struck-by injury from suspended cable or ductwork during installation — risk of head or facial injury
Pinch-point or crush injury to fingers and hands during ductwork or cable-tray assembly — risk of fracture or crush injury
Coordination failure between trades — risk of rework, delay, and repeat exposure to hazards if electrical, data, and HVAC routes conflict
controls: Verify all electrical, data, and HVAC trade routes on marked-up floor plan and 3D model before any installation starts. Resolve conflicts on site with all trades present and document agreement in writing.
Use cable identification tape (colour-coded per AS/NZS 3000) at all cable entry and exit points. Do not route unmarked cable.
Install electrical conduit or cable tray before pulling cable. Do not lay exposed cable in partition cavities or ceiling voids.
Secure all suspended ductwork and cable trays with approved hangers every 1.2 m. Check that hangers are anchored to structural members, not partition frames or services.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (Level 5) and eye protection, conduit, and ductwork edges. Change gloves if cut or torn.
Establish exclusion zone (2 m radius) below all overhead service installation work. Restrict access to authorised workers and alert occupants before work starts.
Brief all trades on pinch-point and crush hazards during ductwork assembly. Demonstrate safe hand position and clearance zone around bending and joining operations.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not route any electrical cable until: licensed electrician has issued isolation certificate confirming cable de-energised and locked-off at source, and plan conflicts have been resolved and documented
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start gyprock facing until: all service rough-ins complete, tested, and signed off in writing by electrical, data, and HVAC trade leads
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unmarked, unidentified, or suspected energised cable is encountered during routing or termination
🛑 STOP WORK if: trade routes conflict on site and cannot be resolved immediately with all trades present
🛑 STOP WORK if: any suspended ductwork or cable tray anchor point shifts, loosens, or shows visible damage during or after installation
admin: Obtain marked-up floor plans and 3D services model from design engineer before work starts.
Schedule pre-installation coordination meeting with electrical, data, and HVAC trade leads. Document agreed routes and sequence.
Maintain cable identification record (location, colour, route, de-energised date, electrician sign-off) on site.
Record all trade sign-offs on service rough-in completion checklist before gyprock commences.
Brief all occupants in building areas where overhead service work is occurring. Display exclusion zone signage.
Report any hazmat discovery (asbestos-containing insulation, lead paint on cable conduit) to project manager immediately.
ppe: High-visibility vest (occupied building, near occupant movement)
Hard hat (ceiling cavity work, suspended load risk)

monitoring.frequency: Before each service routing task and each cable termination

task_blocks_raw.task: Install ceiling panels, gyprock facing, and seals
task_blocks_raw.scope: Install suspended ceiling tiles or panels into grid framework. Install gyprock sheets to partition frames. Seal all partition-to-soffit gaps and service penetrations with fire-rated sealant. Joint tape and finish gyprock seams per specification. Allow compound to cure
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance on ladder or platform while lifting ceiling panels or gyprock sheets — risk of serious injury or death
Gyprock sheet or panel falls from height or during handling — risk of crush injury or head injury to personnel below
Chemical burn from fire-rated sealant contact with skin — risk of dermatitis or respiratory irritation if fumes are inhaled
Muscle strain or back injury during manual handling and installation of heavy gyprock panels — risk of soft-tissue injury or acute strain
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during panel or gyprock installation
controls: Install and secure work platform or scaffolding to grid height before starting. Platform must be stable, level, and rated for full crew weight plus material loads.
Erect exclusion zone below work area. Barricade 2 m radius around all panel and gyprock handling. Post spotter to control access and watch for dropped objects.
check ladder or step stool for damage or defects before use. Secure ladder base with feet on level ground. Only single-person access allowed on ladders.
Wear harness and lanyard clipped to overhead anchor point rated for work load during elevated work above 2 m height.
Check fire-rated sealant SDS on point of use before opening. Confirm ventilation in area is adequate — open windows or activate local exhaust fan.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and hi-viz shirt or vest
Use two-person team for gyprock sheet handling. Use lifting frame or mechanical hoist to raise sheets to height. Never manually lift gyprock above shoulder height.
Secure ceiling panels and gyprock sheets to grid or frame immediately after installation. Do not leave unsupported material at height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install panels or gyprock until: work platform is installed, level, secured, and tagged as safe by supervisor
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply fire-rated sealant until: substrate is clean and dry, SDS Section 8 ventilation requirements are confirmed on site, and chemical PPE is available and worn
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses footing on platform or ladder, or harness anchor point fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: gyprock sheet or panel becomes unstable, drops, or shows signs of falling
🛑 STOP WORK if: sealant fumes cannot be controlled by ventilation or worker reports respiratory irritation or skin contact occurs
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Confirm building occupants are notified of ceiling work, exclusion zone, and sealant cure time before starting.
Record work completion, cure time start, and re-entry approval date on site log.
White Card (CPCCWHS1001) verification — general construction induction completed by all workers on site.

task_blocks_raw.task: Install carpet tiles and floor finishes
task_blocks_raw.scope: Prepare floor substrate — vacuum, remove all dust and debris. Install underlay if required. Lay carpet tiles in specified pattern from centre point outward. Trim edge tiles to suit perimeter and service penetrations. Secure tiles as per manufacturer specification.
hazards: Trip hazard from debris, underlay folds, or uneven floor substrate — risk of slip and fall causing minor injury or fracture
Muscle strain or back injury during kneeling, bending, and manual laying of carpet tiles — risk of soft-tissue injury or acute strain
Exposure to adhesive or bonding-agent fumes during tile installation — risk of respiratory irritation or chemical sensitivity
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Muscle strain or back injury during repetitive installation work
controls: Clear and vacuum floor substrate thoroughly before underlay or tile placement — remove all dust, debris, and loose material.
check floor surface for levelness, cracks, or damage — tell supervisor if substrate varies >3 mm over 3 m or is unsuitable for tile installation.
Lay underlay smoothly without folds or wrinkles — secure edges and seams to prevent trip hazards during tile installation.
Start tile layout from marked centre point — establish grid pattern and confirm alignment before securing any tiles.
Kneel on tile-laying board or kneeling pad — do not work on bare concrete or hard surfaces for extended periods.
Limit repetitive bending and kneeling — rotate task every 30 minutes with posture-neutral task (e.g., measuring, trimming, material staging).
Use handheld tile cutter for edge trims — cut tiles over debris tray to contain dust and fragments; never bend or force tiles by hand.
Apply adhesive or bonding agent per manufacturer SDS — make sure room is ventilated, SDS on point of use, and application limits adhered to.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install underlay or start tiling until: floor substrate is clean, dry, inspected, and levelness confirmed as suitable for installation.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: floor substrate is uneven (>3 mm variation over 3 m), cracked, contaminated, or wet — do not proceed until rectified and approved.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails during adhesive application or room becomes unoccupiable due to fume buildup — resume only when air quality is restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports back pain, muscle strain, or repetitive-strain symptoms — assign alternative task and review work pace and posture.

Record cure times and re-entry restrictions on site signage — post 'Do Not Walk — Curing Tiles' notices until manufacturer cure period is met.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) — if adhesive vapour levels exceed manufacturer threshold or room ventilation is limited.
Safety shoes with good grip — for wet or adhesive-contaminated floor areas.
Knee pads — for kneeling work on hard floors and underlay.

Confirm isolation using a two-point voltage tester on the circuit before touching any conductor or terminal.
Install light fittings and connect to isolated rough-in only. Do not work on energised circuits.
Check each light fitting for secure mounting to ceiling structure before energising circuit.
Test fitting functionality after energisation only when all personnel have vacated the area directly below.
Install HVAC grilles and diffusers to completed ductwork using specified fixing method — verify no loose components before leaving work area.

Barricade area directly below ceiling work to prevent unauthorised entry during fitting installation and testing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not energise any light circuit until: electrical rough-in has been checked for continuity and earth integrity by the electrician, and isolation and two-point test have been verified and recorded by supervisor on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: voltage tester shows supply is not fully isolated before any connection work begins.

Brief all personnel on barricade location and entry prohibition during fitting installation and testing phase.
Record circuit isolation, two-point test result, and fitting functionality test in site logbook with date, time, and tester name.
tell building manager and occupants of temporary supply isolation and expected duration.

check partitions, ceiling, flooring, and fittings against original design drawings and specification — record all defects in writing with location and type.

fix defects using hand tools or approved power tools — do not use power tools in wet areas without RCD protection.

Trip hazard from debris, tools, or temporary protection materials during site cleanup — risk of slip and fall causing minor or moderate injury
Exposure to residual dust and fine particles during final sweeping and cleanup — risk of respiratory irritation or inhalation exposure
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Struck-by injury from falling hoarding sections

Barricade hoarding dismantling zone with caution tape and 'Do Not Enter' signs; prohibit occupants and workers from entering 2 m radius during removal.
Remove hoarding panels systematically from top to bottom; secure each panel as it is loosened to prevent sudden drop or swing onto workers or occupants below.
check each hoarding section and barricade frame for stability, bent fixings, or damage before and during removal; do not force stuck components—obtain supervisor approval to modify or cut fixings.
Place removed hoarding, barricade frames, and temporary bracing in designated waste bin or secure stack away from walkways and occupied zones.
Vacuum common-area floors and Level 3 using HEPA-filtered equipment to remove fine dust and debris; bag and label all waste as construction dust.
Remove all temporary signage, exclusion-zone markers, and caution tape; verify no tripping hazards remain on stairs, doorways, or floor level changes.
Sweep and check final work area for loose nails, screws, or metal fixings; remove or flag any debris before occupant re-entry.

Record final site photographic evidence of cleaned and demobilised areas.
Brief building manager on any outstanding remedial works, cleaning, or post-handover obligations.
